high_level_overview.overview: CBTRN03C is a batch reporting program within the CardDemo credit card management application, operating as part of the transaction processing workflow to produce audit-ready financial reports. It serves the back-office reporting function, transforming raw transaction data into a structured, human-readable detail report for business analysts, auditors, or operations staff. The program reads a sequential transaction file, filters records by a configurable date range, enriches each transaction with descriptive lookups (card-to-account cross-reference, transaction type, and transaction category), and writes a formatted detail report with page-level, account-level, and grand total summaries.

key_features.description: Reads start and end dates from a parameter file to include only transactions processed within the specified reporting period.
Performs random-access lookups against three indexed reference files (card cross-reference, transaction type, and transaction category) to add descriptive labels to each transaction record.
Resolves a card number to its associated account ID using an indexed XREF file, grouping report output by account.
Produces a formatted sequential report file with headers, detail lines, and page totals, resetting every 20 lines per page.
Detects card number breaks and writes account subtotal lines whenever transactions transition from one card number to another.
Accumulates a running grand total across all pages and writes a final grand total line at the end of the report.
Checks file status codes after every I/O operation and abends the program with a diagnostic message if any unexpected error occurs, ensuring data integrity.
Coordinates the opening, reading, and closing of six distinct files (transaction, report, cross-reference, transaction type, transaction category, and date parameters) in a controlled sequence.

input_output.name: TRANSACT-FILE
input_output.description: Sequential transaction file (TRANFILE) - reads transaction records containing transaction ID, type, category, amount, card number, timestamps, and other transaction details for report generation

input_output.name: XREF-FILE
input_output.description: Indexed card cross-reference file (CARDXREF) - randomly accessed by card number to look up associated customer ID and account ID for each transaction

input_output.name: TRANTYPE-FILE
input_output.description: Indexed transaction type file (TRANTYPE) - randomly accessed by transaction type code to retrieve the transaction type description for the report

input_output.name: TRANCATG-FILE
input_output.description: Indexed transaction category file (TRANCATG) - randomly accessed by composite key of transaction type code and category code to retrieve the category description for the report

input_output.name: DATE-PARMS-FILE
input_output.description: Sequential date parameters file (DATEPARM) - reads a single record containing the start date and end date range used to filter transactions included in the report

input_output.name: REPORT-FILE
input_output.description: Sequential report output file (TRANREPT) - writes the formatted daily transaction detail report including page headers, transaction detail lines, page totals, account totals, and grand totals

data_flow.description: Opens all input files (TRANSACT-FILE, XREF-FILE, TRANTYPE-FILE, TRANCATG-FILE, DATE-PARMS-FILE) and output file (REPORT-FILE) with error handling and abend on failure
Reads a single record from DATE-PARMS-FILE into WS-DATEPARM-RECORD to establish the reporting date range filter; abends on read error
Sequentially reads the next record from TRANSACT-FILE into TRAN-RECORD (defined by CVTRA05Y copybook); sets END-OF-FILE flag on EOF
Compares TRAN-PROC-TS (first 10 characters) against WS-START-DATE and WS-END-DATE; records outside the range are skipped via NEXT SENTENCE
Compares TRAN-CARD-NUM against WS-CURR-CARD-NUM; if different and not first time, writes account totals, then updates WS-CURR-CARD-NUM and triggers cross-reference lookup
Performs a random READ on XREF-FILE using FD-XREF-CARD-NUM (set from TRAN-CARD-NUM) to retrieve CARD-XREF-RECORD containing the associated account ID; abends on invalid key
Performs a random READ on TRANTYPE-FILE using FD-TRAN-TYPE (set from TRAN-TYPE-CD) to retrieve TRAN-TYPE-RECORD containing the transaction type description; abends on invalid key
Performs a random READ on TRANCATG-FILE using composite key FD-TRAN-CAT-KEY (FD-TRAN-TYPE-CD + FD-TRAN-CAT-CD) to retrieve TRAN-CAT-RECORD containing the category description; abends on invalid key
On first transaction or when page size (20 lines) is reached, writes report name header, blank line, and two column header lines to REPORT-FILE; also writes page totals before new headers

Initializes TRANSACTION-DETAIL-REPORT, populates it with TRAN-ID, XREF-ACCT-ID, type code, type description, category code, category description, source, and amount, then writes to REPORT-FILE; increments line counter
Adds TRAN-AMT to WS-PAGE-TOTAL and WS-ACCOUNT-TOTAL for each detail line; WS-PAGE-TOTAL is rolled into WS-GRAND-TOTAL and reset at each page break
Writes REPORT-PAGE-TOTALS record with WS-PAGE-TOTAL to REPORT-FILE at each page break; adds page total to grand total and resets page total to zero
When card number changes (and not first time), writes REPORT-ACCOUNT-TOTALS record with WS-ACCOUNT-TOTAL to REPORT-FILE and resets account total to zero
At end of file, writes REPORT-GRAND-TOTALS record with WS-GRAND-TOTAL to REPORT-FILE as the final summary line
Closes all six files (TRANSACT-FILE, REPORT-FILE, XREF-FILE, TRANTYPE-FILE, TRANCATG-FILE, DATE-PARMS-FILE) with error handling and abend on failure

data_dependencies.dependency: Date parameter must be read before transaction processing
data_dependencies.description: WS-START-DATE and WS-END-DATE are populated from DATE-PARMS-FILE in step 0550-DATEPARM-READ before the main processing loop begins; without valid date parameters the program either sets END-OF-FILE to 'Y' (skipping all processing) or abends

data_dependencies.dependency: XREF lookup depends on card number change detection
data_dependencies.description: The cross-reference lookup (1500-A-LOOKUP-XREF) is only triggered when TRAN-CARD-NUM differs from WS-CURR-CARD-NUM, meaning XREF-ACCT-ID used in detail lines is carried over from the previous lookup for all transactions with the same card number

data_dependencies.dependency: Report header write depends on WS-FIRST-TIME flag
data_dependencies.description: Headers are written only on the first call to 1100-WRITE-TRANSACTION-REPORT (WS-FIRST-TIME = 'Y'); the flag is set to 'N' immediately after, so headers are only written once at report start and then at each page break via line counter modulo check

data_dependencies.dependency: Page total must be written before headers on page break
data_dependencies.description: In 1100-WRITE-TRANSACTION-REPORT, 1110-WRITE-PAGE-TOTALS is called before 1120-WRITE-HEADERS when the line counter modulo page size equals zero, ensuring totals from the previous page appear before the new page header

data_dependencies.dependency: Account total write depends on card number sequence
data_dependencies.description: Account totals are written only when a new card number is detected and WS-FIRST-TIME is 'N'; this assumes the TRANSACT-FILE is sorted or grouped by TRAN-CARD-NUM, otherwise account totals will be incomplete or incorrect

data_dependencies.dependency: Transaction type and category lookups depend on valid reference data
data_dependencies.description: TRANTYPE-FILE and TRANCATG-FILE must contain matching records for every TRAN-TYPE-CD and TRAN-TYPE-CD/TRAN-CAT-CD combination present in TRANSACT-FILE; an INVALID KEY condition causes an immediate program abend with no recovery

data_dependencies.dependency: XREF-FILE must contain a record for every card number in TRANSACT-FILE
data_dependencies.description: The READ of XREF-FILE in 1500-A-LOOKUP-XREF uses INVALID KEY to abend the program; there is no soft-error handling, so every card number in the transaction file must have a corresponding cross-reference entry

data_dependencies.dependency: Composite key integrity for TRANCATG-FILE lookup
data_dependencies.description: FD-TRAN-CAT-KEY is built from two separate fields (FD-TRAN-TYPE-CD from TRAN-TYPE-CD and FD-TRAN-CAT-CD from TRAN-CAT-CD); both fields must be correctly populated in TRAN-RECORD before 1500-C-LOOKUP-TRANCATG is called

The ELSE branch of 'IF END-OF-FILE = N' in the main loop executes ADD TRAN-AMT and page/grand total writes when END-OF-FILE is 'Y'; this means the last transaction amount is added to totals in the EOF branch rather than the normal detail path, creating a data flow dependency on the EOF detection timing

data_dependencies.dependency: WS-GRAND-TOTAL accumulation depends on page total writes
data_dependencies.description: WS-GRAND-TOTAL is only incremented inside 1110-WRITE-PAGE-TOTALS; if no page break occurs before EOF, the final page total added in the EOF branch must also flow through 1110-WRITE-PAGE-TOTALS to be included in the grand total

data_dependencies.dependency: All files must be successfully opened before processing begins
data_dependencies.description: All six OPEN statements are performed sequentially before any data is read; failure of any open causes an immediate abend via 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM, so all files are a hard prerequisite for execution

error_handling.description: All six files (TRANFILE, REPTFILE, CARDXREF, TRANTYPE, TRANCATG, DATEPARM) follow an identical pattern: APPL-RESULT is pre-set to 8 before the OPEN, then set to 0 on success or 12 on failure. If not APPL-AOK, a descriptive DISPLAY message is issued, the file status is moved to IO-STATUS, 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS is performed, and 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM is called. All file open errors are fatal and immediately terminate the program.

For TRANSACT-FILE (1000-TRANFILE-GET-NEXT) and DATE-PARMS-FILE (0550-DATEPARM-READ), file status is evaluated using EVALUATE: '00' maps to APPL-RESULT=0 (success), '10' maps to APPL-RESULT=16 (EOF), and any OTHER maps to APPL-RESULT=12 (error). EOF sets END-OF-FILE='Y' to gracefully terminate the main loop. Any other read error triggers a DISPLAY message, IO-STATUS population, 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS, and 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM for a fatal termination.

Random reads against XREF-FILE (1500-A-LOOKUP-XREF), TRANTYPE-FILE (1500-B-LOOKUP-TRANTYPE), and TRANCATG-FILE (1500-C-LOOKUP-TRANCATG) use the INVALID KEY clause. When a key is not found, a DISPLAY message identifies the invalid key value, IO-STATUS is set to 23 (a standard VSAM not-found code), 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS is performed, and 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM is called. All invalid key conditions are treated as fatal; there is no soft-error or skip logic for missing reference data.

In 1111-WRITE-REPORT-REC, after each WRITE to REPORT-FILE, TRANREPT-STATUS is checked: '00' sets APPL-RESULT=0, anything else sets APPL-RESULT=12. If not APPL-AOK, 'ERROR WRITING REPTFILE' is displayed, TRANREPT-STATUS is moved to IO-STATUS, 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS is performed, and 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM is called. All write errors are fatal.

All six close routines (9000–9500) follow the same pattern as open routines: APPL-RESULT is pre-set to 8, then evaluated after CLOSE. A status of '00' resets APPL-RESULT to 0; otherwise it is set to 12. Failures trigger a descriptive DISPLAY, IO-STATUS population, 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS, and 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM. Close errors are fatal. Note: 9000 and 9100 use arithmetic idioms (ADD 8 TO ZERO, SUBTRACT APPL-RESULT FROM APPL-RESULT) functionally equivalent to MOVE.

9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS provides a centralized status decoder. If IO-STATUS is non-numeric or IO-STAT1='9' (indicating a system/hardware error), it extracts the binary second byte via TWO-BYTES-BINARY redefinition to produce a numeric status code displayed as IO-STATUS-04. For standard numeric statuses, it formats and displays the two-byte code in a four-character field. This routine is always called before abending to provide diagnostic detail.

9999-ABEND-PROGRAM provides a single centralized abend routine. It displays 'ABENDING PROGRAM', sets TIMING=0 and ABCODE=999, then calls the IBM Language Environment routine 'CEE3ABD' to force a controlled abnormal termination with a user abend code of 999. This ensures the job step fails with a recognizable abend code and that upstream job schedulers or JCL can detect the failure.

Within the main processing loop, transactions whose TRAN-PROC-TS falls outside the WS-START-DATE to WS-END-DATE range are silently skipped using NEXT SENTENCE. This is not an error condition per se but represents the only non-fatal data-level filtering; no message is logged for out-of-range transactions.
